inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,942 normalized logical lines. The source develops a lattice quantization of the inverse Berry–Keating Hamiltonian, maps each inverse-model eigenstate to a zero-energy threshold state of a Russian-doll model, connects exact solvability to cyclic renormalization, derives the smooth Riemann zero-counting term as a regulator-dependent spectral deficit, documents why simple level deformations do not recover fluctuations, and proposes level-dependent I± couplings whose continuum limits become partner scattering potentials. Formula extraction is generally recoverable from prose and equation context; plot/diagram interiors are separately marked defective.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic identity and compact statement of the inverse-lattice, missing-state, exact-solvability, and cyclic-RG claims.

sections_inspected.label: I. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Sets the Hilbert–Pólya/Berry–Keating target, distinguishes smooth and fluctuating spectral information, and motivates the inverse-Hamiltonian bridge to the Russian-doll model.

sections_inspected.label: II. Hamiltonians: overview and Berry–Keating model
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the BK→I→RD architecture, contrasts Berry–Keating and Connes regularizations, and generalizes xp to v(x)p.

sections_inspected.label: II.B. Inverse Hamiltonian
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs the finite lattice inverse operator, explains the renormalization coupling and boundary-condition role, and checks continuum recovery despite finite-dimensional commutator defects.

sections_inspected.label: II.C. Russian doll Hamiltonian
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the RD model and gives the exact nonunitary map from inverse-model eigenstates to RD threshold states.

sections_inspected.label: III. Continuum limit
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Solves the continuum integral equation, derives boundary quantization, and reframes the spectrum as a free particle in an adapted logarithmic coordinate.

sections_inspected.label: IV. Renormalization group analysis
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives exact RG closure, its cyclic continuum flow, state-dependent periods, Russian-doll scaling, and the relation between state labels and cycle counts.

sections_inspected.label: V. Exact solution
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives the discrete recursion and product quantization, proves completeness, extracts the Gamma-function finite count, compares regulators, and audits failed attempts to model zero fluctuations.

sections_inspected.label: VI. The I± models
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces the two RG-stable level-dependent coupling patterns and derives their continuum partner-potential representations and open scattering/integrability questions.

sections_inspected.label: VII. Conclusions and prospects
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recapitulates the cutoff-dependent missing-state interpretation and the proposed move from level changes to level-dependent couplings.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliography only; inspected for the terminal source boundary and excluded from semantic units.

accepted_units.title: Invert xp before quantizing it
accepted_units.why_material: The source isolates the failure point of the formal Berry–Keating proposal and makes the central representation move: quantize 1/(xp) on a lattice, where the inverse momentum has a tractable Green kernel, rather than impose an unestablished direct quantization of xp.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the spectral motivation and the exact point at which inversion is proposed; later lines supply the construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low formula risk: the decisive strategy is explicit in prose; xp and 1/xp notation is legible.

accepted_units.title: Cyclic RG suggests a Russian-doll bridge, but exponent and energy roles must be repaired
accepted_units.why_material: Compares scale-related RD bound states and Dirichlet-like wavefunctions with Berry–Keating dilation eigenfunctions, identifies two mismatches, and proposes the inverse Hamiltonian as the mechanism that resolves them rather than treating surface resemblance as an equivalence.
accepted_units.context_note: Self-contained motivation for why the superconducting model enters; the exact map is established later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula risk: exponents and scaling factors are text-extracted but supported by adjacent prose.

accepted_units.title: BK→I→RD as a regularization, RG, and threshold-state pipeline
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the roles of the three models: BK supplies the dilation target, I supplies a finite-dimensional regularization with a running boundary coupling, and RD supplies cyclic RG and threshold states corresponding to I eigenstates.
accepted_units.context_note: An overview unit; later units provide exact definitions and derivations without changing this division of labor.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: the architecture and coupling roles are recoverable from prose despite equation typography.

accepted_units.title: Berry–Keating phase-space truncation recovers only the smooth counting asymptotics
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how a Planck-cell phase-space cutoff produces the leading smooth Riemann counting formula, explicitly separates smooth and oscillatory terms, and records that this is heuristic rather than a spectrum obtained from a consistent quantized xp operator.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the needed counting formulas and the limitation that motivates the lattice construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: displayed integrals and constants have extraction risk, but the asymptotic agreement and heuristic limitation are stated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Connes cutoff reverses emission into missing states
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts a large phase-space cutoff with Berry–Keating's Planck cell: the divergent continuum count contains the Riemann smooth term with the opposite sign, motivating zeros as absences in a continuum rather than emitted eigenlines; it also ties the formal xp eigenfunctions to scale generation.
accepted_units.context_note: The figure interior is not needed; the prose, caption, formulas, and formal operator supply the comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: phase-space formulas are degraded in places, but the sign, divergence, and missing-state interpretation are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Replace x by a velocity profile v(x) without losing adapted plane-wave structure
accepted_units.why_material: Generalizes xp to v(x)p and gives both its cutoff count and formal eigenfunction in the integrated coordinate ∫dx/v(x), anticipating the later coordinate that turns the inverse-model spectrum into free motion.
accepted_units.context_note: Requires the monotone positive v(x) assumptions stated at the start of the span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: exact integral placement is formula-dependent but legible enough to recover the representation change.

accepted_units.title: Finite lattice Green kernel regularizes the inverse Berry–Keating operator
accepted_units.why_material: Uses the one-dimensional Green function for p⁻¹ to define a finite Hermitian matrix with weights f_n and an additional coupling g_I, then defines the regularized BK Hamiltonian by matrix inversion.
accepted_units.context_note: The extra coupling is retained because later RG elimination generates it; the pure BK choice is its zero value.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: matrix entries and normal ordering depend on extracted equations, but surrounding prose fixes their meaning.

accepted_units.title: Finite matrices violate the canonical commutator yet recover it spectrally in the continuum
accepted_units.why_material: Makes the finite-dimensional obstruction explicit through the trace of [X,P], then uses convergence of most commutator eigenvalues to justify continuum recovery; it also clarifies that the RG coupling is classically invisible but quantum-mechanically fixes boundary conditions.
accepted_units.context_note: Starts with the figure caption that states the spectral convergence and includes the interpretive prose following it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low to moderate: the graph itself is unnecessary; caption and prose support the claim.

accepted_units.title: An inverse-model eigenstate is a zero-energy RD threshold state
accepted_units.why_material: After defining the RD Hamiltonian, a nonunitary wavefunction rescaling converts each I eigenproblem into an RD problem at zero energy, with the BK energy determining the time-reversal-breaking RD coupling and the velocity levels becoming RD energies.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes definitions, equations, normalizability contrast, classical check, and the exact scope of the state-by-state map.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula risk: parameter identifications are equation-dependent but remain recoverable from prose and aligned displays.

accepted_units.title: Differentiating the inverse integral equation recovers generalized BK eigenfunctions
accepted_units.why_material: Transforms the continuum integral equation into a first-order differential equation whose solution, after undoing the RD rescaling, exactly matches the formal generalized Berry–Keating eigenfunction.
accepted_units.context_note: The span includes the integral equation, change of variables, differentiation, and recovered solution.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: integral bounds and exponents rely on formula extraction, but the equality with the earlier eigenfunction is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Boundary quantization becomes a twisted free particle in an adapted coordinate
accepted_units.why_material: Boundary ratios yield the energy quantization condition; for uniform levels the spectrum becomes continuous as the cutoff grows, while q=log n—and more generally q=∫dn/ε(n)—turns the states into plane waves in a box with coupling-controlled twist.
accepted_units.context_note: Combines quantization, continuum limitation, scalar product, and the generic adapted coordinate needed for the RG comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: several displayed equations are required, but each conclusion is restated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Gauss elimination closes exactly only after retaining the boundary coupling
accepted_units.why_material: Eliminating the highest component reproduces the same Hamiltonian family: h_I and level weights remain invariant while g_I flows. Reparameterizing by the associated RD threshold state exposes the exact state-conditioned RG rule.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the reason g_I must be part of the model rather than an optional decoration.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the rational flow equation is formula-dependent but supported by the explicit closure statement.

accepted_units.title: The spectral coordinate and RG scale are complementary, yielding energy-dependent cycles
accepted_units.why_material: The continuum flow is a tangent trajectory; the scaling coordinate s equals total adapted length minus q, and the I-model RG period is 2πℏ/E, unlike the energy-independent period of a fixed RD model.
accepted_units.context_note: Begins after the extraction-defective diagram and includes the flow, coordinate relation, and contrast.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: flow and period formulas are legible; prose states the energy dependence.

accepted_units.title: One RG cycle lowers the state label, separating gapless I scaling from gapped RD scaling
accepted_units.why_material: Splitting the quantization integral at one cycle proves an energy/state relabeling identity. Its state-dependent contraction gives algebraic, gapless inverse-model levels, whereas the fixed RD cycle produces exponentially scaled bound states.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both the derivation and the gapped-versus-gapless comparison; the figure is not needed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: exponent typography is fragile, but the algebraic-versus-exponential contrast is explicit.

accepted_units.title: The quantum number counts completed RG cycles to leading order
accepted_units.why_material: Relates the finite number of cycles to system-size contraction and shows that the state label approximately equals the number of cycles needed to reach one site, while flagging finite-size corrections as potentially important.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the bridge from cyclic flow to the later smooth zero-counting interpretation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low to moderate: the iteration formula is extracted, but the correspondence and its asymptotic status are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Discrete recursion produces a product quantization condition and a complete spectrum
accepted_units.why_material: Subtracting neighboring RD threshold equations yields an exact recursion; one boundary condition closes it into a product equation whose phase is monotone and spans exactly N integer labels, establishing completeness of the finite regularized BK spectrum.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the alternative RG-solvability rationale, recursion, boundary closure, log form, and completeness argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate to high formula dependence, but the recursion and monotonicity/completeness conclusions are readable and corroborated by prose.

accepted_units.title: Exact momentum spectrum diagnoses which term survives the continuum limit
accepted_units.why_material: A constant-level special case gives the exact finite momentum spectrum, and expansion of the general phase count shows that only the harmonic-like sum ∑1/ε_n diverges for uniform levels, explaining why the first continuum term controls large N.
accepted_units.context_note: Combines a solvable calibration case with the precise asymptotic truncation criterion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: tangent and series expressions are formula-dependent but supported by the stated continuum conclusion.

accepted_units.title: The smooth Riemann term is a finite spectral deficit, but its linear term is cutoff-scheme dependent
accepted_units.why_material: Taking the continuum limit of the exact phase count reproduces Connes's finite smooth term up to a regulator-dependent linear contribution; incompatible naive cutoff identifications prevent a conclusive equivalence and motivate a blueshift interpretation of missing states in a fixed energy window.
accepted_units.context_note: Preserves the failed cutoff matching rather than silently identifying the regularizations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: coefficients depend on formulas, while the mismatch and blueshift interpretation are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Uniform levels turn the finite count into the Gamma phase of the smooth Riemann formula
accepted_units.why_material: Renormalizing the exact finite product gives a Gamma-function phase. Choosing the zero-point shift a=−3/4 aligns its Gamma term with the smooth Riemann count, while the remaining linear and constant pieces expose boundary and regulator choices.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the product limit, Gamma identity, spectral interpretation of the shift, and the precise comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence: signs, shifts, and Gamma arguments should be checked against the retained PDF before downstream exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Zeta regularization converts the missing linear term into a scale choice
accepted_units.why_material: Regularizing the infinite product assigns the disputed linear contribution to the regulator μ; choosing μ=1/π restores the Riemann linear term while leaving a separate half-unit boundary mismatch.
accepted_units.context_note: This resolves the earlier coefficient discrepancy only within a chosen scheme, not by proving cutoff equivalence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence: the infinite-product regularization and scale exponent require scan verification for exact constants.

accepted_units.title: A half-cycle offset improves smooth zero locations but leaves random fluctuations unexplained
accepted_units.why_material: The finite numerical check compares the smooth count at known zeros and finds a half-unit offset consistent with completed RG cycles; the remaining deviations track the oscillatory zeta contribution, so the uniform model is explicitly limited to the smooth component.
accepted_units.context_note: Plot pixels are extraction-defective, but the tested quantity, sample scope, mean, mean-square, and conclusion are stated in text and caption.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: table rows and plot layout are degraded; use the prose/caption for the qualitative result and verify numbers from the PDF if reused.

accepted_units.title: Level perturbations and prime deletion cannot synthesize zero-scale randomness from smooth phase steps
accepted_units.why_material: Records two negative routes—algebraic corrections to levels and deleting prime-indexed levels—and explains their common obstruction: sums of smoothly varying arctangent contributions resist producing the irregular interpolant required by the zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both attempted modifications, their asymptotic effects, and the mechanism-level reason for failure.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the modified Gamma formula is fragile, but the negative findings and smooth-superposition obstruction are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Only two level-dependent coupling patterns preserve the simple antisymmetric interaction under RG
accepted_units.why_material: Promotes the scalar g coupling to a structured matrix and identifies max-index and min-index patterns I+ and I− as the two choices that keep the h interaction invariant. Their elimination directions are opposite, and the exact I↔RD threshold-state map survives levelwise.
accepted_units.context_note: The diagram interior is degraded, but equations, caption, and prose specify the matrices and RG directions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: max/min definitions are legible; figure geometry is not required.

accepted_units.title: The I+ continuum equation becomes scattering from the derivative of the running coupling
accepted_units.why_material: Introducing an integrated wavefunction converts the nonlocal threshold equation into a second-order ODE; an adapted coordinate and gauge transformation expose an effective Schrödinger Hamiltonian with potential V+=(1/2)dg_D/dq and explicit boundary conditions.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the constant-coupling plane-wave limit as a consistency check against the earlier quantization condition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence: derivative signs, gauge phase, and boundary conditions should be scan-checked before exact formal reuse.

accepted_units.title: I− supplies the opposite derivative potential and a constrained route to oscillatory scattering data
accepted_units.why_material: The companion construction gives V−=−(1/2)dg_D/dq with reversed boundary placement. The source then proposes, without claiming success, that scattering from these potentials or discrete couplings might carry the oscillatory count and perhaps connect RG-time asymmetry to GUE behavior.
accepted_units.context_note: Separates derived partner structure from speculative Riemann/GUE prospects.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate to high: the partner sign and boundary formulas are extracted but readable; the research claims are explicitly conjectural.

accepted_units.title: Statewise solvability does not automatically extend to many-body integrability
accepted_units.why_material: Limits the exact correspondence: multiple rapidities obstruct a direct many-body I→RD map, and level-dependent boundary couplings suggest a more complicated transfer-matrix structure rather than an established integrable theory.
accepted_units.context_note: Useful guardrail against promoting one-particle exact solvability into a broader result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: the limitation is stated in prose.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Inversion as a quantization bridge rather than a spectral equivalence
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Passing to the inverse converts a problematic dilation Hamiltonian into a Green-kernel lattice operator; the RD threshold map then supplies exact solution machinery, while the continuum limit recovers the original generalized BK wavefunctions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The map is state-dependent and nonunitary, and recovery of formal wavefunctions does not establish that Riemann zeros are eigenvalues.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: One adapted coordinate unifies spectral phase and cyclic RG
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The coordinate q=∫dn/ε and RG scale s=L−q make boundary phase quantization and cyclic coupling flow complementary descriptions; one state-conditioned cycle lowers the spectral label.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The cycle period depends on the selected I-model energy, unlike a single fixed RD Hamiltonian, and the label/cycle equality is leading-order before finite-size corrections.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Smooth zero counting is a regulator-conditioned deficit signal
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Exact phase counting yields the Gamma-function smooth Riemann term as a finite deficit or blueshift of continuum states, with the disputed linear coefficient controlled by regularization scale and a half-cycle offset improving the sampled smooth locations.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Cutoff schemes are not proven equivalent, the numerical check uses known zeros, and none of this produces the oscillatory zeta term or proves RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The failure of level engineering motivates coupling-derived scattering potentials
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Smooth arctangent contributions explain why perturbing or deleting levels fails to model irregular zero fluctuations; imposing RG closure instead selects two level-dependent coupling patterns whose gradients become partner scattering potentials.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source proposes the scattering connection but gives neither discrete exact eigenvalue equations for I± nor a construction reproducing the zeros.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Exact one-particle structure carries an explicit many-body boundary
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Threshold-state correspondence and discrete recursion make the one-particle inverse model exactly solvable, but the mechanism relies on a single spectral parameter and does not directly survive multiple rapidities.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Many-body integrability of I or I± remains an open question rather than an inherited consequence of RD integrability.
